newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat rallies amid mixed indications.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat rallies amid mixed indications.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures rallied slightly on Monday in rising volume, with 39 contracts changing hands.
January and March 1998 both traded higher, by A$1.50 a tonne to A$170.00 and by A$1.00 to A$172.00 respectively. Most other settlement prices were up by about A$4.00 a tonne.

Gary Booth of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures said the market rose on statements at the International Grains Council meeting in London by Australian Wheat Board chairman Trevor Flugge that world wheat demand would exceed market expectations.
Good inquiry emerged on Monday from traders and end-users, supported by light grower hedging, he said. The weaker Australian dollar also continued to support the market.

As dry conditions in southern Australia continued, demand for grain for stock feed was increasing while crop prospects diminished. Rain was still needed in southern Australia to establish the crop, he said.
Analysts believed the market should bottom around its present level, he said.
"It's feeling a little better even though it is still in its bearish trend," Booth said.
